question.text:
The electronic configurations of bivalent europium and trivalent cerium are:
(atomic number: Xe=54 , Ce=58 , Eu=63)

options.text: <math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></math>

<math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>

<math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mn>6</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mn>6</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>

<math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow></msup></math>

solution.text:
Electronic configuration of Ce and Eu in ground state are following:

Ce=Xe 4f1 5d1 6s2Eu=Xe 4f7 6s2

Trivalent cerium means cerium loss three electrons and obtain +3 charge and bivalent Europium means Europium loss two electrons and obtain +2 charge, so their electronic configurations are following

Eu2+:Xe4f7


Ce3+:Xe4f1
